capabilities: scan installed plugins' main.js for dangerous API patterns
verify plugin bundles against GitHub release hashes
score each plugin's risk on a 0-100 scale with tiers
show findings in a sortable in-vault report panel
detect newly installed plugins and offer to scan them
disambiguation: An audit tool, not a firewall or antivirus: it flags and scores plugins but never disables them or sandboxes anything.
extras: Desktop-only (isDesktopOnly: true), no mobile support. README explicitly warns static analysis has blind spots and cannot catch all malicious plugins. No telemetry, no premium tier. Unauthenticated GitHub API is rate-limited to 60 requests/hour; a personal access token raises this to 5000/hour.
motivation: The author built it because Obsidian cannot sandbox community plugins, leaving users exposed to plugins with full file, network and shell access.
problem: Obsidian cannot sandbox community plugins, so every enabled plugin gets full access to files, network and shell commands with no way for users to assess the risk.

relations.evidence: The only outbound calls are to api.github.com (to fetch release metadata and asset hashes).

requires.name: GitHub fine-grained personal access token (read-only, no scopes)

summary: Security audit tool that scans installed community plugins' main.js for dangerous APIs, verifies hashes against GitHub releases, and scores risk.
